He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne Dukes]] and the [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU Mustangs]]. ==Early life== Mike grew up in [[Scarborough, Toronto]].{{cite web |last1=Reynolds |first1=Kevin |title=How Isiaha Mike has transformed into SMU's unquestioned leader |url=https://247sports.com/college/smu/Article/Isiaha-Mike-SMU-basketball-Tim-Jankovich-138786062/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=August 5, 2020 |date=November 18, 2019}} As a middle schooler, Mike stood 6'5 and spent much time in the gymnasium to compensate for his lack of basketball skills. He played [[pick-up game|pick-up]] basketball in middle school but switched his focus to academics while attending [[West Hill Collegiate Institute]] in [[Scarborough, Toronto]]. Mike played for Hoops Canada Elite on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) circuit.{{cite web |last1=Wolstat |first1=Ryan |title=Isaiah Mike has bright future in basketball |url=https://torontosun.com/2014/08/20/isiaha-mike-has-bright-future-in-basketball/wcm/49ed91b8-50c6-4172-9631-5a0e1fbc6647 |website=[[Toronto Sun]] |accessdate=August 5, 2020 |date=August 21, 2014}} In August 2014, he won [[most valuable player]] of the Americas Team Camp. He later transferred to Trinity International School in [[Las Vegas|Las Vegas, Nevada]] under head coach Greg Lockridge.{{cite web |last1=Reynolds |first1=Kevin |title="Destined To Do": Inside Isiaha Mike’s Rise, Leadership and Future |url=https://www.smudailycampus.com/sports/destined-to-do-inside-isiaha-mikes-rise-leadership-and-future |website=The Daily Campus |accessdate=August 5, 2020 |date=April 1, 2020}} He averaged 27.6 points, 14.3 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 1.9 steals per game as a senior. He led his team to a second straight National Christian School Athletic Association title game and was named to the All-Tournament Team.{{cite web |title=Isiaha Mike |url=https://smumustangs.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/isiaha-mike/10258 |publisher=SMU Athletics |accessdate=August 5, 2020}} Mike played in the [[BioSteel All-Canadian Basketball Game|BioSteel All-Canadian Game]] in April 2016.{{cite web |title=Maker headlines Biosteel All-Canadian roster |url=https://www.tsn.ca/maker-headlines-biosteel-all-canadian-roster-1.466415?tsn-amp |publisher=[[The Sports Network]] |accessdate=August 5, 2020 |date=April 7, 2016}} North Pole Hoops ranked him the third-best Canadian player in the 2016 class behind [[Thon Maker]] and [[Justin Jackson (basketball, born 1997)|Justin Jackson]].{{cite web |title=Isiaha Mike |url=https://goduquesne.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/isiaha-mike/31 |publisher=Duquesne University Athletics |accessdate=August 5, 2020}} ==College career== Mike played for [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne]] in his freshman season. He averaged 11.3 points and 5.8 rebounds per game and was named to the [[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] All-Rookie Team. After the season, he was granted a release from the program following the departure of head coach [[Jim Ferry]].{{cite web |last1=Labedz |first1=Grant |title=Duquesne’s Isiaha Mike granted release to transfer |url=https://www.a10talk.com/duquesnes-isiaha-mike-granted-release-transfer/ |publisher=A10 Talk |accessdate=August 5, 2020 |date=April 3, 2017}}{{cite web |last1=DiPaola |first1=Jerry |title=In wake of success, ex-Duquesne forward Isiaha Mike regrets transferring |url=https://archive.triblive.com/sports/college/duquesne/in-wake-of-success-ex-duquesne-forward-isiaha-mike-regrets-transferring/ |website=[[Pittsburgh Tribune-Review]] |accessdate=August 5, 2020 |date=February 2, 2018}} Mike transferred to [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU]] during his official visit, turning down an offer from [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]]. He sat out one season due to [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] transfer rules and was a member of the [[practice squad|scout team]] during practice. At first, Mike was frustrated with his role, arguing with the coaching staff, but matured with the help of his teammate [[Jarrey Foster]]. On January 30, 2019, he scored a career-high 25 points and grabbed seven rebounds in an 85–83 loss to [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]]. Mike finished the season averaging 11.7 points, 5.4 rebounds, 1.7 assists and 1.1 blocks per game. As a junior, Mike matched his career-high of 25 points, all of which came after the first half, and grabbed 12 rebounds in an 87–85 double overtime loss to [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]] on December 20.{{cite web |title=SMU Loses 2OT Heartbreaker At Georgia, 87–85 |url=https://smumustangs.com/news/2019/12/20/mens-basketball-smu-loses-2ot-heartbreaker-at-georgia-87-85.aspx |publisher=SMU Athletics |accessdate=August 5, 2020 |date=December 20, 2019}} In his junior season, he averaged 14 points, 6.3 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 1.4 steals per game and was named to the Third Team All-[[American Athletic Conference]]. Mike announced that he would remain in the [[2020 NBA draft]] and forgo his senior season.{{cite web |last1=Sayles |first1=Damon |title=SMU forward Isiaha Mike discusses move to 'go all in' on turning pro |url=https://smu.rivals.com/news/smu-forward-isiaha-mike-discusses-move-to-go-all-in-on-turning-pro |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |accessdate=August 5, 2020 |date=July 8, 2020}} ==Professional career== === Niners Chemnitz (2020–2022) === On August 31, 2020, Mike signed his first professional contract with [[Niners Chemnitz]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]].{{cite web |title=Das letzte Puzzleteil |url=https://www.chemnitz99.de/news/585/Das-letzte-Puzzleteil |publisher=[[Niners Chemnitz]] |accessdate=September 2, 2020 |language=German |date=August 31, 2020}} He averaged 10.5 points and 5.2 rebounds per game. On July 3, 2021, Mike re-signed with the team.{{cite web |title=Isiaha Mike re-signs with Niners Chemnitz |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/isiaha-mike-re-signs-with-niners-chemnitz/ |website=Sportando |access-date=July 3, 2021 |date=July 3, 2021}} === Scarborough Shooting Stars (2022–2023) === On May 29, 2022, Mike signed with the [[Scarborough Shooting Stars]] of the [[CEBL]].{{Cite instagram|user=scarboroughshootingstars|postid=CeJlvxtFYvf|title=Isiaha Mike/ Forward |date=May 29, 2022|accessdate=May 30, 2022}} === JL Bourg (2022–2024) === On June 30, 2022, Mike signed with [[JL Bourg Basket|JL Bourg]] of the French [[LNB Pro A]].{{Cite web |date=2022-06-29 |title=Isiaha Mike rejoint aussi le club Bressan Mozzart Bet]] of the [[ABA League]], [[Basketball League of Serbia]] (KLS) and the [[EuroLeague]].{{cite web|title=Crno-bela simfonija: Nova energija i duh tradicije Partizana na ulasku u sezonu During the 2024–25 season, Partizan managed to lift the record eighth [[2024–25 ABA League First Division|ABA League]] championship, and the [[2024–25 Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian League]] championship, the first one after 11 seasons. === Bayern Munich (2025–2026) === On August 25, 2025, Mike signed with [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL) and the [[EuroLeague]] until 2027.{{Cite web |title=Isiaha Mike Joins Bayern Munich |url=https://www.pianetabasket.com/en/isiaha-mike-joins-bayern-munich-339826 |access-date=2025-08-25 |website=Pianeta Basket |language=en}} === Bahçeşehir Koleji (2026–present) === On July 1, 2026, Mike signed a one–year contract with [[Bahçeşehir Koleji S.K.|Bahçeşehir Koleji]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{cite web|title=Isiaha Mike is back in the EuroCup with Bahcesehir|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/eurocup/news/isiaha-mike-is-back-in-the-eurocup-with-bahcesehir/|website=euroleaguebasketball.net|date=July 1, 2026|access-date=July 1, 2026}}
